grades.reason: Shows that after open() followed by unlink(), the inode persists without a name and is only cleaned up when the process closes the fd or exits. This partly explains why the file stays usable after unlink. It does not explicitly mention reading or link counts.

grades.quote: The operating system removes the file when it no longer has any names and is no longer in use by any process. (An open file can continue to exist without any names, as you can demonstrate in Exploration Project 8.10.)
grades.reason: Directly explains that unlink only removes a name. The file itself is removed only when it has no names and no process is using it, so an open file survives unlink. It also covers the other cause: additional hard links under other names.
